rationale: Amplitude's docs confirm feature-experiment capabilities including running A/B tests, defining goal metrics, and measuring 'causal lift' with visual editors and flag-based rollouts, indicating experimentation and results measurement exist. Amplitude offers a documented MCP server and AI feature that lets users ask plain-language growth questions grounded in behavioral data, plus REST/Dashboard APIs to pull chart/query data programmatically, directly supporting agent-driven Q&A. However, this is an Amplitude-hosted analytics model rather than warehouse-native SQL access, and no independent evidence confirms real-world reliability of the MCP/AI answers, with community feedback questioning data accuracy generally.

Direct probes confirm llms.txt (HTTP 200) and docs.md are live and served, plus an OpenAPI spec and an official MCP server for AI tool integration, directly satisfying the agent-oriented docs story.
